# Coder

Dimension: Coder (github.com/coder/coder) as a self-hosted Kubernetes workspace
platform for Claude Code sessions. Sources: [`citations.md`](../citations.md) [1]–[6].

## License & single-user gating

Coder core is AGPL-3.0 [1]. The free Community edition has **no caps** a single
operator cares about: "Unlimited workspaces and templates" and "Unlimited members
within a single organization", and lists "Desktop and web-based IDEs" in both tiers
[3]. The relevant Premium (paid) gates are HA ("multiple Coder server replicas"),
"Resource quotas per organization and user", workspace proxies, multi-org controls,
and >1 external auth integration [3]. **"Browser-only connections is a Premium
feature"** [2] — i.e. *enforcing* browser-only (disabling SSH/desktop tunnels) is
paid, though the web terminal and web IDEs themselves are usable in Community.

## Embedded Tailscale vs the external TS Operator (decision-critical)

Coder embeds a Tailscale-derived mesh: "Tailscale's open source backs our
websocket/HTTPS networking logic" and "By default, your Coder server also runs a
built-in DERP relay" [2] — so coderd does not depend on a Coder-hosted coordinator.
Crucially for browser use: **"Direct connections via the web browser are not
supported"** and **"The coder servers relays dashboard-initiated connections between
the user and the workspace"** [2]. So browser code-server/web-terminal traffic is
plain server-relayed HTTP through coderd's dashboard — **the operator/client never
runs a Coder Tailscale client**, and you can front coderd's HTTP dashboard with the
existing TS Operator and leave Coder's mesh unused for browser access.

The mesh is not *disabled*, only bypassed for browser traffic. A real collision is
documented: issue #15523 — Coder's default `10.10.10.0/24` workspace subnet conflicts
with an existing company Tailscale, breaking P2P (Nov 14 2024, closed via PR #18323)
[6]. For browser-only use this is moot (everything relays), but it confirms the
two-Tailscale interaction is a known sharp edge.

## The HTTP-only TS Operator clash (decision-critical)

Coder's web IDEs (code-server, etc.) via `coder_app` subdomains require a wildcard
hostname **and** a matching wildcard TLS cert: "Wildcard access URLs require a TLS
certificate that covers the wildcard domain" [5]. The operator's TS Operator exposes
a single `<name>.<tailnet>.ts.net` HTTP-only Service with no wildcard subdomains and
no TLS [42] — so **subdomain-based code-server access does not fit**. Path-based app
sharing is the fallback but the docs warn "Most applications are designed to work at
the root of a hostname", breaking Vite/React/Next.js/JupyterLab [5]. The built-in
**web terminal** is served by coderd itself (no wildcard) and is the reliable browser
path — sufficient for the `claude` TUI, but code-server-in-browser is impractical
under HTTP-only single-hostname ingress.

## Storage, templates, sidecar

The official k8s template uses `access_modes = ["ReadWriteOnce"]` [4] — a direct fit
for Longhorn. Workspaces are provisioned by coderd's built-in Terraform provisioner;
**Terraform is required per workspace type** (authored once) [4]. The workspace is a
`kubernetes_deployment_v1`; code-server is installed in the agent `startup_script`,
and a sidecar (e.g. the operator's OAuth-refresh container) can be added as a sibling
container [4].

## Counter-evidence

Coder's own positioning and third-party reviews skew enterprise; HA is Premium-only
(a single free coderd replica despite a 3-node HA cluster) [3]. The Terraform-per-
workspace model and external Postgres add Day-2 burden disproportionate to one
operator. The web-IDE wildcard-TLS requirement is the concrete misfit with the
HTTP-only TS Operator [5][42].

## Gaps / limitations

- External Postgres requirement and the absence of a documented Coder + Argo CD + TS
  Operator + Longhorn reference are Snippet-level (discovery agents), not fetched.
- No fetched confirmation that the **web terminal** is contractually a Community
  feature (strongly implied — not in any Premium list [3] — but not stated verbatim).
- No documented hard switch to *remove* the embedded mesh (only bypass via browser).
